recreation_brief:
1. Set the slide background to light gray (#F2F2F2).
2. Draw the outer frame: a thin dark-red (#AA0000) rectangle outline, no fill, around the entire slide perimeter.
3. Place the title 'Data Overfit and Underfit' in a centered text box in the top ~10% of the slide, large bold sans-serif, dark red (#B00000).
4. Draw a filled yellow (#FFFF99) circle in the top-right corner with the text '19' centered on it in black (#000000).
5. Draw the content box: a large rectangle with a dark-red (#AA0000) border and no fill, spanning ~15-90% of slide height and nearly the full slide width; steps 6-12 are placed inside it.
6. Place the row label 'Classification' at the far left of the upper row (band ~15-60% of slide height) in blue (#0000CC) bold italic sans-serif.
7. Build scatter panel 1 as the first of three equal side-by-side panels to the right of the 'Classification' label: plain x/y axes with unlabeled ticks on a white (#FFFFFF) background; red (#FF0000) 'X' markers clustered lower-left; gray (#808080) 'O' markers upper-right; a straight diagonal blue (#0000FF) decision-boundary line between the two clusters; below the panel, bold black caption 'Under-fitting' with smaller black sub-caption '(too simple to explain the variance)' beneath it.
8. Build scatter panel 2 in the middle position with the same axes and marker setup as step 7: a smooth, gently curved blue (#0000FF) decision boundary; below the panel, the bold black caption 'Appropriate-fitting' (no sub-caption).
9. Build scatter panel 3 in the right position with the same axes and marker setup as step 7: a highly wiggly blue (#0000FF) decision boundary looping around individual points; below the panel, bold black caption 'Over-fitting' with smaller black sub-caption '(forcefitting -- too good to be true)' beneath it.
10. Place the row label 'Regression' at the far left of the lower row (band ~62-90% of slide height) in blue (#0000CC) bold italic sans-serif.
11. Build the left regression chart in the left half of the lower row, to the right of the 'Regression' label: a rectangle with light-green (#CCFFCC) fill and dark-red (#AA0000) border; axes labeled 'y' (vertical) and 'x' (horizontal); black (#000000) circle data points along a curve; a smooth thin orange (#FF6600) 'Target' curve; a smooth blue (#0000FF) 'Fit' curve that deviates from the target at the right end; a legend in the panel's top-right corner with entries 'Data' (circle marker), 'Target' (thin line), 'Fit' (line).
12. Build the right regression chart in the right half of the lower row: a rectangle with light-green (#CCFFCC) fill and dark-red (#AA0000) border; axes labeled 'y' (vertical) and 'x' (horizontal); black (#000000) circle data points; a smooth green (#00CC66) '2nd Order Fit' curve; a red (#FF0000) wiggly '10th Order Fit' curve that passes through every data point and oscillates wildly at the panel edges; a legend in the panel's bottom-right corner with entries 'Data', '2nd Order Fit', '10th Order Fit'.
